The retrieved evidence shows two incompatible sets of findings on whether testosterone increases prostate cancer risk. Several large, high-credibility studies report that higher circulating or genetically predicted free testosterone is associated with increased prostate cancer risk, including overall, aggressive, and early-onset disease [d1, d2]. Conversely, other high-credibility cohort studies and meta-analyses find no association between higher testosterone levels and prostate cancer risk, and state that testosterone therapy does not increase risk [d3, d11, d14, d8, d15]. These mutually exclusive conclusions indicate genuine disagreement in the research literature.
